 How to Address the City Council

  residence in order to speak. Each person addressing the Council is generally given up to
 three minutes to speak (with double the time allotted to non-English speakers using a
 translator). The amount of time authorized may be adjusted by the chair. If you wish to

 computer, please click the "raise your hand" button. Press *6 to un-mute yourself, state

 equipment to present electronic material during meetings is not allowed.

 City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-5151 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

 Your courtesy is requested to help our meetings run smoothly. Please follow these
 simple rules so we can make the best possible use of your time and ours:

  Please refrain from public displays or outbursts, such as unsolicited applause,

FROM:  CITY MANAGER’S OFFICE – FINANCE DIVISION
DISTRICT:  ALL
SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY AND QUARTERLY INVESTMENT
  ACTIVITY REPORTS FOR DECEMBER 2022

ISSUE
Receive and file the monthly and quarterly investment activity reports for December
2022.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council accept the monthly and quarterly investment
activity reports for City of Palmdale and Successor Agency for December 2022.

BACKGROUND
Pursuant to Section 16 of the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency Investment
Policy, the City Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on
investments to the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors.
The reports shall detail the type of investment, name of the issuer, purchase date, date
of maturity, amount of deposit, and rate of interest. This information shall be provided
for all City and Successor Agency pooled investments, as well as for Certificates of
Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts and
Community Facilities District accounts which are managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly and quarterly reports provide a synopsis of the investment activity for the
City of Palmdale and Successor Agency. The reports provide information on assets,
allocations, average maturities, yields, and book valuations.
The interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report.

The market values presented for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are
based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This
information was obtained from the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets,
Capital Market Finances, or other reliable source of market prices.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Report on Investments
February 1, 2023
Page 2

DISCUSSION
Compliance with Investment Policy

For December, the invested portfolio amount for the City of Palmdale totaled
$272,105,998 a decrease of $13,534,260 from the previous month, and an increase of
$39,785,215 in comparison to last year. The monthly decrease is monthly due to
quarterly debt service payments made during the month.

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of December was $7,253,780. The
balance increased by $1,128,742 from the last month due to a sale of a Successor
Agency property that occurred during the month.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs,
Corporate Notes, U.S. Treasury Securities and Government Agency Paper, each
adhering to portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entity’s investment policy to 1)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations; 2) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient
liquidity to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash
requirements; and 3) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive
market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on, is providing liquidity to measure
up to the City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the Finance
Department is currently investing in two pooled funds, LAIF and CAMP. These are
intended for the daily operational activities, used for economic uncertainties and
maintenance needs. The pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the
City and Successor Agency meet cash flow requirements.

Total LAIF balance for the City of Palmdale at the end of December is $102,258,780, a
decrease of $8,000,000 due to withdrawals to cover operational expenditures.

Successor Agency LAIF balance at the end of December was $4,432,717, no changes
compared to the prior month.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Report on Investments
February 1, 2023
Page 3

CAMP’s balance for City of Palmdale at the end of December is $253,089 compared
to November balance of $252,167 a slight increase due to interest earned. The
interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report. As of December 31, 2022, the interest rates for LAIF and CAMP investments
were at 2.173 percent and 4.30 percent, respectively. By comparison, the LAIF and
CAMP interest rates at the end of November were at 2.007 percent and 3.90 percent.
Both rates have slightly increased within this month. This time last year, LAIF and
CAMP rates were at 0.212 percent and 0.05, respectively.

The chart above shows both the Local Agency Investment Fund and California Asset
Management Program’s average monthly yields beginning March 2022 through
December 2022.

We anticipate that rates will begin to level off in the upcoming months, considering the
current state of the economy. In recent months, CAMP shows better performance than
LAIF in interest rates. The difference between the performance of the two funds is
partly due to the varying pool characteristics. CAMP’s portfolio composition is much
more subject to market volatility, resulting in performance variation.

Diversity

The Finance Division aims to diversify the investment portfolios to avoid incurring
unreasonable and avoidable risks regarding specific security types or individual
financial institutions.

City of Palmdale and Successor Agency’s investment portfolios remain strongly
diversified. The monthly and quarterly reports include all investments held by both
entities and current book values as of December 31, 2022.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Report on Investments
February 1, 2023
Page 4

It is anticipated that both the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency will have
sufficient moneys to meet its expenditure requirements for the next 6 months as we
continue to monitor any financial impact due to the Coronavirus pandemic and the
current economic conditions and the impact on interest rates.

Attached are summaries of the investments on the City of Palmdale and Successor
Agency’s books as of December 31, 2022.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with the recommended actions for this report.

STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  B. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.
  C. Involve and expand engagement to enhance public oversight and
  transparency.

ISSUE
Should the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-005, a Resolution of the City
Council of the City of Palmdale approving and authorizing the execution and delivery of
a Supplemental Agreement No. 6 to Amended and Restated Fiscal Agent Agreement
related to Community Facilities District No. 93-1 (Ritter Ranch), and authorizing actions
related thereto?

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-005, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
  Palmdale approving and authorizing execution and delivery of a Supplemental
  Agreement No. 6 to Amended and Restated Fiscal Agent Agreement related to
  Community Facilities District No. 93-1 (Ritter Ranch), and authorizing actions
  related thereto.
BACKGROUND
In 1994, the City Council formed the City of Palmdale Community Facilities District No.
93-1 (Ritter Ranch), and in 1995 the City issued special tax bonds for the Community
Facilities District to finance various public infrastructure improvements within and in the
vicinity of the proposed Ritter Ranch development. The prior owner of the Ritter Ranch
property, Ritter Holdings LLC, failed to make required special tax payments due in
February of 2020, and its lender, Preston Hollow Capital, LLC (Preston Hollow), which
also is the owner of the special tax bonds, foreclosed on the Ritter Ranch property and
became the owner of the Ritter Ranch property and all of the rights and interests of Ritter
Holdings, LLC under agreements with the City and others related to Ritter Ranch.
Preston Hollow subsequently transferred the Ritter Ranch property to RdR Development
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Documents Related to Ritter Ranch
February 1, 2023
Page 2

Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“RdR”), of which Preston Hollow is
the sole member.

On September 1, 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 2020-091, pursuant to
which, at the request of Preston Hollow, it approved a supplement to the Amended and
Restated Fiscal Agent Agreement pursuant to which the special tax bonds were issued,
to defer payments otherwise due on the special tax bonds during the period from March
1, 2020 to and including March 1, 2022 to allow time for Preston Hollow and RdR to
determine the actions needed to commence development of the Ritter Ranch property.
That Resolution also approved a Deposit Agreement (A-7107) between the City and
Preston Hollow (the “Deposit Agreement”) pursuant to which Preston Hollow advanced
funds to pay costs of the City and its consultants related to requests by it and RdR
relative to the development of the Ritter Ranch property. To date, Preston Hollow had
advanced a total of $806,097 to the City to be used as provided in the Deposit
Agreement, including City actions related to the current request to process a supplement
to the agreement pursuant to which the special tax bonds were issued.

On February 2, 2022, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2022-016, pursuant
to which, at the request of RdR, it approved another supplement to the Amended and
Restated Fiscal Agent Agreement to defer interest payments due on the special tax
bonds on September 1, 2022 and March 1, 2023 to September 1, 2023 and the principal
due on the Bonds on September 1, 2022 to September 1, 2024, all to allow additional
time for Preston Hollow and RdR to continue actions needed to move forward with the
development of the Ritter Ranch property.

DISCUSSION
Since their obtaining ownership of the Ritter Ranch property, Preston Hollow and RdR
have proceeded to take actions necessary to restart the development of Ritter Ranch.
RdR has now requested in a petition submitted to the City Council that the City agree to
again amend the documents for the special tax bonds to defer bond payments otherwise
due on September 1, 2023 and March 1, 2024 to September 1, 2024 and to change the
due date for the special tax payment needed to pay the rescheduled debt service due
on the Bonds on September 1, 2024 to August 30, 2024, all in order to allow them
additional time to take the actions needed to continue the development of the property.

The City Council is now requested to approve a supplement to the agreement
governing the special tax bonds to defer payments on the bonds. The supplement has
been prepared by the City’s bond counsel, Quint & Thimmig LLP, and has been
reviewed by City Finance Department Staff and the Interim City Attorney.

FA Agreement.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION DECLARING OPPOSITION TO THE MASS
  IMPORTATION OF THE UNHOUSED FROM ANY JURISDICTION
  INTO THE CITY OF PALMDALE

ISSUE

Discussion and possible action declaring Palmdale’s opposition to the mass importation
of the unhoused from any jurisdiction into the City of Palmdale.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the proposed resolution declaring its
opposition.

BACKGROUND

Cities throughout Los Angeles County, following the example set by the City of Los
Angeles and the County of Los Angeles, have declared a state of emergency related to
homelessness.

Emergency declarations allow government entities to demand that departments identify
all city-owned properties that can be used for some form of housing. Specifically, within
Palmdale’s city limits, the City of Los Angeles owns approximately 17,000 acres of bare
land with few if any improvements in and around the Plant 42 installation.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution Opposing Mass Importation of Unhoused to Palmdale
February 1, 2023
Page 2

DISCUSSION

There exists little to no infrastructure or services in place to effectively manage and assist
in addressing this crisis. The City of Palmdale is opposed to the idea that any jurisdiction
could export homelessness problems on Palmdale’s working class, family-oriented desert
community on an emergency basis, without allowing time for community and cross-
agency communications. Rather, time should be taken to collaborate on equitable,
community-based solutions to address this humanitarian crisis, locally and regionally.

Procedural History

At the December 21, 2022, the City Council majority concurred that Los Angeles should
not export their homeless problem to Palmdale, and declined to adopt a resolution to
declare a city state of emergency in Palmdale.

At the January 11, 2023 meeting, the City Council directed staff to return with a revised
resolution with specified language. The proposed resolution includes all such language.
The resolution also includes the following additional clause, at the request of Mayor Pro
Tem Alarcón: “WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale seeks to open the lines of communication
between the City of Los Angeles and the City of Palmdale to support one another in our
respective efforts in addressing the multi-faceted issues of the unhoused in each of our
cities.”

None.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF PALMDALE CALIFORNIA DECLARING ITS
  OPPOSITION TO THE MASS IMPORTATION OF THE
  UNHOUSED FROM ANY JURISDICTION INTO THE
  CITY OF PALMDALE

  WHEREAS, the Los Angeles Times has reported that there are currently more than
42,000 people who are homeless in the City of Los Angeles;

  WHEREAS, other agencies/jurisdictions own approximately 17,000 acres of
undeveloped land with few if any improvements in and around Palmdale’s Plant 42
installation;

  WHEREAS, it is currently unclear as to exactly what actions any jurisdiction would
take to attempt to resolve the homeless crisis, and whether, or to what extent their powers
might be used to create a homeless “village” in Palmdale or its vicinity;

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale supports taking well-reasoned and long-term
solutions to the ongoing issues relating to housing and homelessness;

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale opposes short-term solutions which, when not
properly planned, can cause multiple negative and unplanned secondary impacts which
can cause significant legal issues; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale seeks to open the lines of communication
between the City of Los Angeles, the County, and other stakeholders to support one
another in our respective efforts in addressing the multi-faceted issues of the unhoused
in each of our cities.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. Declaration of Opposition. For the above reasons, the City Council
declares its opposition to the mass importation of the unhoused from any jurisdiction into
the City of Palmdale.

  SECTION 2. Certification. The City Clerk shall certify to the passage and adoption
of this resolution.

ISSUE
Approve Agreement with Berry Dunn McNeil & Parker, LLC, for consulting services for
the development of a Parks and Recreation Master Plan.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8182, with Berry Dunn McNeil & Parker, LLC, for the
  development of a Parks and Recreation Master Plan; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute the Agreement with Berry
  Dunn McNeil & Parker, LLC, including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The City of Palmdale currently does not have a Parks and Recreation Master Plan, which
is needed to further assess and implement a plan to guide decision-making for the
development and management of parks, recreation facilities and services. Park Master
Plans are common planning tools in many municipalities, and as part of the City’s General
Plan update, the Parks, Recreation and Open Space element lists development of a parks
and recreation plan as a top priority. The General Plan states that a Parks and Recreation
Master Plan is needed to address park conditions and needs, recreation programming,
facilities, and funding opportunities. Additionally, the Plan will evaluate adopted park
standards, including designations for type of parks and guidelines for the facilities to be
developed in future parks.

On May 25, 2022, the Measure AV Oversight Committee was presented the budget for
the development of a Parks and Recreation Master Plan and was unanimously approved
and adopted by the City Council on June 29, 2022, for Fiscal Year 2022/2023.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Parks Master Plan Agreement A-8182
February 1, 2023
Page 2

DISCUSSION
The RFP for the Parks and Recreation Master Plan was released on June 28, 2022, with
a closing date of August 10, 2022. The RFP was viewed by 67 vendors, and based off
commodity codes, was sent to 1,004 vendors. The scope of work for this Parks and
Recreation Master Plan includes the professional services necessary to develop a
standard and strategized plan for the Parks and Recreation Master Plan. Scope of work
is as outlined below:

Community Engagement:
   To identify, describe, and implement a comprehensive strategy and methodology
  for community involvement.
   To engage community members through a minimum of eight facilitated
  workshops, the execution of a statistically valid survey, and partner and City
  Council presentations.
   To provide written records and summaries of results for public retention.

Resource and Data Collection
   Conduct statistically valid survey to provide random samples from community.
   Conduct analysis and assessment of parks, green spaces, programs, recreation
  centers, and services.
   Conduct analysis and assessment of department current level of programs,
  events, services, and maintenance to relate to current and future goals and
  objectives.
   Compile inventory and assessment of existing spaces.

Project Timeline
   Proposed project schedule with milestones and objectives; to include
  engagement meeting timeframes.

Deliverables and Strategy
   Plan to include written goals, objectives, policy statements, a financial and action
  plan to articulate a roadmap and made for department’s future.
   Develop an action plan to include strategies, priorities and an analyst of budget
  support and funding mechanisms for all terms, in all spaces.
   Develop a strategy to implement goals and policies from the City’s General Plan.
   Prioritize recommendations for needs.
   Identify areas of service shortfalls and projected impact of future trends.
   Prepare maintenance management plan and identify performance
  measurements.
   Review and discuss existing funding mechanisms and cost recovery practices.
   Prepare Park development standards and incorporate City of Palmdale preferred
  design specifications.

BACKGROUND
Mrs. Perez has been serving in the role of Interim City Manager since March 2022 and
prior to was named Acting City Manager in December 2021. The City Council met in
closed session on January 11, 2023 and provided a 5-0 positive performance evaluation
of Ronda Perez. Subsequently, on January 18, 2023 they again met in closed session
to discuss filling the City Manager position permanently. They agreed that Ronda Perez
should be appointed City Manager, thus removing the Interim title.

The Employment Agreement before the Council this evening is entered into with Mrs.
Perez effective January 18, 2023 in an effort to provide stability and consistency in the
executive leadership of the organization.

  1. The Term of this initial Agreement will be for a period of three (3) years ending
  January 18, 2026. The Agreement provides for two (2) optional two-year
  incremental extensions (Section 2).
  2. Employee is at-will and serves at the pleasure of a majority of the City Council
  and shall be entitled to 12 months severance pay provided termination occurs
  without cause as outlined in the Agreement (Section 4).
